changes.comment: Pick up the @rx-controls/react useControlEffect fix, and stop cancelling useValueChangeEffect's pending debounced call on unmount. v4 applied debounce with useDebounced, which owns a useRef and registers no cleanup, so a pending call outlived the component; the cleanup added here looked tidier and silently dropped exactly the work these effects stage on the last edit — an autosave, a validation round-trip — whenever the subtree went away inside the debounce window. The callbacks normally write controls that outlive the component, so firing late is meaningful rather than a leak into a dead tree. Both were found as silent regressions in a real app on the v4 to v5 bump, where a validation POST simply never happened.
